title: Tax first or tax last?
hook: Pay tax now and the growth is tax-free. Or let more money grow, and pay at the end?

knows: a flat tax rate takes the same share of any amount
doesNotKnow: that paying a flat tax before growth or after growth gives the same amount when the two rates are equal, because the order of multiplying does not matter; only the difference between today's rate and the later rate decides

misconception: Paying the tax now is better, because then all the growth is tax-free (or the mirror: deferring is better, because more money is growing).
objective: The learner can explain that $10,000 taxed 25% then grown 4×, and grown 4× then taxed 25%, both end at $30,000 because both are $10,000 × 0.75 × 4, and that only a different later rate makes one bigger.

claims.text: At 25% tax now and 25% later with 4× growth, both accounts end at $30,000: A pays $2,500 up front and its $7,500 grows to $30,000; B grows $10,000 to $40,000, then hands a quarter back.
claims.source: A = 10,000 × 0.75 × 4 = 30,000; B = 10,000 × 4 × 0.75 = 30,000; B's tax = 40,000 × 0.25 = 10,000 (Demo.tsx accA(), accB(); builder node run, 2026-10-14). Brief: company/domains/briefs/economics.md #57. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: A = 10,000 × 0.75 × 4 = 30,000 (tax 2,500 up front, 7,500 grows to 30,000); B = 10,000 × 4 = 40,000, tax 10,000 (a quarter), keeps 30,000. Reveal needs milestone question (×4, 25%); q = accA(4) = 30,000.

claims.text: Both are $10,000 × 0.75 × 4, multiplied in a different order; for any growth, equal flat rates give equal results.
claims.source: (1 − t) × G = G × (1 − t) for any growth factor G (commutativity). The stage's ×2 chip shows the same tie at $15,000. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. (1 − t) × G = G × (1 − t) for any G: equal flat rates tie at every growth. Stage ×2 at 25% shows A $15,000 and B $15,000.

claims.text: Only a change of rate decides it: with 4× growth, at a 35% later rate B ends at $26,000 and at 15% at $34,000, against A's $30,000 (the reveal quotes the learner's own recorded rate and growth).
claims.source: B = 10,000 × G × (1 − later): ×4 at 35% = 26,000, at 15% = 34,000, at 30% = 28,000; ×2 at 35% = 13,000 vs A 15,000 (Demo.tsx accB(); builder node run). The reveal prints the record set at milestone 'rate', which the record row under the chart also shows. QA path ends at 35%, ×4. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED. Numbers hold (own node: ×4 at 35% B = 26,000, at 15% 34,000; ×2 at 35% B = 13,000 vs A 15,000). But the claim says the reveal quotes the learner's recorded rate and growth, and it prints only the rate: 'at a {rec.later}% later rate, B ended at {rec.b} against A's {rec.a}'. rec is the latest state with a later rate ≠ 25%, at whatever growth was set. The stage opens at ×2, and a learner who moves the slider at ×2, or switches growth after moving it, gets e.g. 'at a 35% later rate, B ended at $13,000 against A's $15,000'. That comes right after 'Both ended at $30,000 … $10,000 × 0.75 × 4', with no ×2 shown, so it reads as if A were $15,000 at ×4. Fix (builder): print the growth in the reveal (e.g. 'at ×{rec.g} and a {rec.later}% later rate'), or record the rate milestone only at ×4. Blocks publishing. | Builder fix v2 (2026-10-14, W-500): the reveal now prints the recorded growth as well as the rate: 'at ×{rec.g} and a {rec.later}% later rate, B ended at {rec.b} against A's {rec.a}' (fallback ×4, 35%, $26,000, $30,000), so a record made at ×2 reads 'at ×2 and a 35% later rate, B ended at $13,000 against A's $15,000'. Claim text unchanged; it already says the reveal quotes rate and growth. Needs a fresh fact-check.

claims.text: The tax system is made up: flat rates, today 25%, no contribution limits, fees or penalties; not advice about any real account.
claims.source: Stage chip 'Model: made-up flat tax. Today 25%. Later: slider.' and the reveal's last sentence. Lesson rule. No real account (e.g. any national tax-advantaged account) is named, per the brief. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Stage chip reads 'Model: made-up flat tax. Today 25%. Later: slider.'; the reveal ends 'Not advice about any real account.'; accA/accB contain no limits, fees or penalties; no real account named. Convention.

recall.question: Two savers each put away $5,000. The flat tax is 20% both now and later, and both get the same growth. One pays the tax first; the other pays it on withdrawal. Who ends with more?
options: The one who paid on withdrawal
recall.why: Taxing then growing is 5,000 × 0.8 × G; growing then taxing is 5,000 × G × 0.8. The same multiplication in a different order, so only a change in the rate could separate them.
